# nagios_host (Resource)

Manages a Nagios XI host.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nagios_host" "example" {
  host_name              = "web01.example.com"
  address                = "10.0.0.10"
  alias                  = "Web Server 01"
  max_check_attempts     = "3"
  check_period           = "24x7"
  notification_interval  = "30"
  notification_period    = "24x7"
  contacts               = ["nagiosadmin"]
  templates              = ["generic-host"]
  notes                  = "Primary web server"
  active_checks_enabled  = true
  passive_checks_enabled = true

  free_variables = {
    "_environment" = "production"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address` (String) The IP address of the host
- `check_period` (String) The time period during which active checks of the host can be made
- `contacts` (Set of String) The list of users that Nagios should alert when a host is down
- `host_name` (String) The name of the host
- `max_check_attempts` (String) How many times to retry the host check before alerting when the state is anything other than OK
- `notification_interval` (String) How long to wait before sending another notification to a contact that the host is down
- `notification_period` (String) The time period during which notifications can be sent for a host alert

### Optional

- `action_url` (String) URL to a third-party documentation repository containing actions to take in the event the host goes down
- `active_checks_enabled` (Boolean) Sets whether or not active checks are enabled for the host
- `alias` (String) A longer name to describe the host
- `check_command` (String) The name of the command that should be used to check if the host is up or down
- `check_freshness` (Boolean) Sets whether or not freshness checks are enabled for the host
- `contact_groups` (Set of String) A list of the contact groups that should be notified if the host goes down
- `coords_2d` (String) The coordinates to use when drawing the host in the statusmap CGI (Nagios's own API field name is 2d_coords, but Terraform attribute names can't start with a digit)
- `coords_3d` (String) The coordinates to use when drawing the host in the statuswrl CGI (Nagios's own API field name is 3d_coords, but Terraform attribute names can't start with a digit)
- `display_name` (String) Another name for the host that will be displayed in the web interface. If left blank, the value from `host_name` will be displayed
- `event_handler` (String) The command that should be run whenever a change in the state of the host is detected
- `event_handler_enabled` (Boolean) Sets whether or not event handlers should be enabled for the host
- `first_notification_delay` (String) The amount of time to wait to send out the first notification when a host enters a non-UP state
- `flap_detection_enabled` (Boolean) Sets whether or not flap detection is enabled for the host
- `flap_detection_options` (Set of String) Determines what flap detection logic will be used for the host. One or more of the following valid options can be provided: 'd' down, 'o' up, or 'u' unreachable.
- `free_variables` (Map of String) A key/value pair of free variables to add to the host. The key must begin with an underscore.
- `freshness_threshold` (String) The freshness threshold used for the host
- `high_flap_threshold` (String) The maximum threshold that should be used when detecting if flapping is occurring
- `hostgroups` (Set of String) A list of hostgroups this host should be a member of, assigned from the host side (complements a hostgroup's own `members` attribute)
- `icon_image` (String) The icon to display in Nagios
- `icon_image_alt` (String) The text to display when hovering over the icon
- `initial_state` (String) The state of the host when it is first added to Nagios. Valid options are: 'd' down, 's' up or 'u' unreachable
- `low_flap_threshold` (String) The minimum threshold that should be used when detecting if flapping is occurring
- `notes` (String) Notes about the host that may assist with troubleshooting
- `notes_url` (String) URL to a third-party documentation repository containing more information about the host
- `notification_options` (String) Determines when Nagios should alert if a host is one or more of the following option: 'o' up, 'd' down, 'u' unreachable, 'r' recovery, 'f' flapping or 's' scheduled downtime
- `notifications_enabled` (Boolean) Determines if Nagios should send notifications
- `obsess_over_host` (Boolean) Sets whether or not Nagios 'obsesses' over the host using the ochp_command
- `parents` (Set of String) A list of hosts that are used to determine the network reachability of this host - if a parent host is down or unreachable, this host is marked unreachable rather than down
- `passive_checks_enabled` (Boolean) Sets whether or not passive checks are enabled for the host
- `process_perf_data` (Boolean) Determines if Nagios should process performance data
- `register` (Boolean) Determines if the host will be marked as active or inactive
- `retain_nonstatus_information` (Boolean) Sets whether or not non-status related information should be kept for the host
- `retain_status_information` (Boolean) Sets whether or not status related information should be kept for the host
- `retry_interval` (String) How often should Nagios try to check the host after the initial down alert
- `stalking_options` (String) A list of options to determine which states, if any, should be stalked by Nagios
- `statusmap_image` (String) The name of the image that should be used in the statusmap CGI in Nagios
- `templates` (Set of String) A list of Nagios templates to apply to the host
- `vrml_image` (String) The image that will be used as a texture map for the specified host

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Hosts can be imported by their host_name.
terraform import nagios_host.example web01.example.com
```
